{"body":"## Summary

Audit and fix every README, manifest Quick Start, describe string, error message, codegen template and plan doc that showed or implied a plaintext secret. Every secret now reaches an extension through `swamp vault put <vault> <KEY>` and `${{ vault.get("<vault>", "<KEY>") }}`.

- **Generators (cloudflare, datadog, snyk, griptape, falai):** each README has a Credentials section. Describe strings and errors point to the vault first; env-var fallbacks stay in code but are documented as discouraged. Secret arguments are marked sensitive, and secrets that APIs return are stored in a vault through sensitive resource fields. All 79 generated extensions were regenerated from the pinned specs the committed code came from, so no upstream API drift is included.
- **Hand-written:**
  - terraform `read_state` masks `sensitive_values`, and terraform-drift reports masked values as unverifiable.
  - teams `bootstrap` stores the refresh token in a vault under a fixed key.
  - exe-dev no longer echoes token output in errors.
  - artifactory, reddit, gcp, azure and the vault extensions used reference syntax that swamp does not support (`vault://`, `<vault:…>`, `{{ vault }}`); those examples now use `vault.get`.
  - Datastore docs use `vault.get` in `.swamp.yaml` and `SWAMP_DATASTORE`.
- **Repo guidance:** new "Secrets Come From a Vault (HARD RULE)" section in `CLAUDE.md` and `.kiro` steering.

**Behavior changes (called out in each extension's release notes):**
- Models whose resources now hold a vaulted secret require a vault before swamp will run their methods.
- The tunnel token resource changes from a string to `{ value }`.
- Secrets inside lists are dropped, because swamp cannot vault fields inside arrays.

**Out of scope, by decision:** all `*-datastore-bootstrap` extensions are untouched and go in a separate PR.

121 extensions are bumped, each with release notes. A local adversarial review ran one full round, and all of its findings were fixed.

# Swamp

## Core Concepts

- **Behaviors** (formerly models) — typed resource definitions exposing methods
  (create, stop, destroy, sync). `swamp behavior` is the preferred spelling;
  every `swamp model` spelling still works (see
  [references/behavior/reference.md#compatibility](references/behavior/reference.md#compatibility)).
- **Data** — versioned state snapshots produced by method runs; referenced via
  CEL expressions.
- **Workflows** — declarative DAGs chaining behavior methods with guard
  expressions for idempotent execution and assert steps for validation.
- **Vaults** — secret storage referenced by behaviors at runtime.
- **Extensions** — TypeScript packages adding behavior types, vault backends,
  datastores, reports, and webhook handlers.
- **Grants** — authorization rules for swamp serve access control.
- **Serve** — exposes the repo over the network with TLS and authentication.

## Routing Table

Route to the right guide based on what the user needs.

| User intent                                                      | Guide                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Behaviors — create, run, edit, delete, search types              | [references/behavior/guide.md](references/behavior/guide.md)                   |
| Workflows — create, run, validate, DAG, history                  | [references/workflow/guide.md](references/workflow/guide.md)                   |
| Data — list, query, versions, GC, delete                         | [references/data/guide.md](references/data/guide.md)                           |
| Vaults — create, store/read secrets, expressions                 | [references/vault/guide.md](references/vault/guide.md)                         |
| Reports — run, configure, view, filter                           | [references/report/guide.md](references/report/guide.md)                       |
| Repository — init, upgrade, datastores, sources                  | [references/repo/guide.md](references/repo/guide.md)                           |
| Extensions — create behaviors/vaults/datastores/reports/webhooks | [references/extension/guide.md](references/extension/guide.md)                 |
| Publishing — push extensions to registry, deprecate              | [references/extension-publish/guide.md](references/extension-publish/guide.md) |
| Issues — file bugs, features, security reports                   | [references/issue/guide.md](references/issue/guide.md)                         |
| Run tracking — active runs, stale detection, diagnostics         | [references/behavior/guide.md](references/behavior/guide.md)                   |
| Architecture — which primitive to use, design trade-offs         | [references/architecture/guide.md](references/architecture/guide.md)           |
| Sharing — promote solo repo to team, datastore + vault setup     | [references/share/guide.md](references/share/guide.md)                         |
| Serve — auth, grants, access control, tokens, OAuth              | [references/serve/guide.md](references/serve/guide.md)                         |
| Troubleshooting — errors, health checks, diagnostics             | [references/troubleshooting/guide.md](references/troubleshooting/guide.md)     |

## Common Commands

```bash
# Behaviors
swamp behavior create <type> <name>            # create a behavior definition
swamp behavior run @<type> <method> <name>     # run a method on a behavior
swamp behavior get <name> --json               # inspect current behavior state
swamp behavior type search [query]             # find available behavior types
swamp behavior list                            # list all behaviors in the repo

# Data
swamp data list <name>                         # list data versions for a behavior
swamp data query '<CEL predicate>'             # query data with CEL expressions
# read one item's latest content (`swamp data get` is deprecated)
swamp data query 'behavior("<name>") && name == "<data>"' --select content

# Workflows
swamp workflow create <name>                   # create a new workflow
swamp workflow validate <name>                 # validate DAG before running
swamp workflow run <name>                      # execute a workflow
swamp workflow run <name> --input key=value    # execute with inputs
swamp workflow resume <name>                   # resume a suspended workflow
swamp workflow resume <name> --run <id>        # retry a failed run's failed steps
swamp workflow resume <name> --from <step>     # re-enter failed run at step
swamp workflow history search --json           # search run history

# Run tracking
swamp run history                              # recent runs (last 24h)
swamp run history --active                     # what's running right now?
swamp run doctor                               # diagnose stale/orphaned runs
swamp run doctor --fix                         # auto-reap stale runs

# Vaults, Reports, Extensions
swamp vault create <type> <name>               # create a vault for secrets
swamp report run <name>                        # run a report
swamp extension push manifest.yaml             # publish an extension
```

## Workflow

1. **Route** — match intent to a guide in the routing table.
2. **Load** — read the guide; load its `reference.md` if needed, deeper
   `references/` only when the guide says to.
3. **Validate** — before running any workflow: `swamp workflow validate <name>`.
   Before destructive methods (delete, stop, destroy):
   `swamp behavior get <name> --json` to confirm the target exists and is in the
   expected state. Proceed only when validation passes.
4. **Verify args** — run `swamp help <subcommand>` (e.g.
   `swamp help behavior run`) to confirm exact flags and arguments before
   executing. The output is structured JSON — the canonical CLI schema. Do not
   guess flags from memory.
5. **Execute** — run the command.
6. **On failure** — load
   [references/troubleshooting/guide.md](references/troubleshooting/guide.md)
   and diagnose before retrying or changing definitions.

## Rules

1. **Use the routing table, not memory.** Don't answer from cached knowledge
   about swamp commands — always load the current guide.
2. **Consult the architecture guide for design decisions.** Before choosing
   between primitives (behavior vs. workflow vs. extension vs. report) or
   explaining a design trade-off, load
   [references/architecture/guide.md](references/architecture/guide.md) and cite
   the design doc you relied on.
3. **Use swamp commands, don't go around them.** Query data with
   `swamp data query`, not by grepping `.swamp/` files. Interact with resources
   through behavior methods, not raw CLI tools when a behavior type already
   wraps the API — check with `swamp behavior type search`. Composing with
   `--json` output (e.g. piping through `jq`) is fine — the anti-pattern is
   bypassing swamp entirely.

# Swamp Issue Skill

Fetch issue details, submit bug reports, feature requests, and security
vulnerability disclosures through the swamp CLI. When logged in
(`swamp auth login`), issues are submitted directly to the swamp.club Lab. When
not logged in, the user is prompted to log in or send via email. The `--email`
flag skips straight to a pre-filled email.

To view an existing issue, use `swamp issue get <number>` — this fetches and
displays the issue's title, type, status, author, body, assignees, and comment
count.

To edit an existing issue's title, body, or type, use
`swamp issue edit <number>`. This opens `$EDITOR` pre-filled with the current
title, type, and body. Use `--title`, `--body`, and/or `--type` flags to skip
the editor. Only the issue author (or admins) can edit. Authors can change the
type to `security` to restrict visibility, but cannot change it back from
`security` — only admins can de-escalate.

## Ownership Classification

Before filing any report (bug, feature, or security), classify where the issue
lives:

1. **Swamp's own CLI/binary** — file against swamp itself with no `--extension`
   flag.
2. **A third-party published extension you don't control** — file with
   `--extension <name>` to route it to that extension's publisher.
3. **An extension you (or the human you're working with) are actively developing
   in this repo's own source tree** — this is not a ticket. Fix the code
   yourself, or ask the human how they want it handled. Do not file an issue.

This step is mandatory. Do not skip it — even if you just filed a legitimate
swamp bug, re-classify before every subsequent report. The failure mode this
prevents is pattern-matching from one correct filing to subsequent incorrect
ones without re-checking the premise.

With `--extension <name>`, reports are routed to the extension's publisher
instead — either as a tagged swamp.club Lab issue (for `@swamp/*` extensions) or
to the publisher's declared repository (for third-party extensions).

To follow up on an existing Lab issue (e.g. add a related finding, link a
sibling issue, or update reproduction steps discovered later), use
`swamp issue ripple <number>` — this posts a comment ("ripple") on the issue.
`swamp issue comment` is an alias for `ripple`. Add `--close` to close the issue
after posting, or `--reopen` to reopen it.

**Verify CLI syntax:** Always run `swamp help issue` to confirm exact flags
before executing — the output is structured JSON.

## Commands

`bug`, `feature`, and `security` support interactive mode (opens `$EDITOR` with
a template) and non-interactive mode with `--title` and `--body` flags. `ripple`
takes a positional issue number and either opens the editor or accepts `--body`
directly.

| Command                       | Purpose                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `swamp issue search [query]`  | Search or list issues by keyword, with optional `--type`, `--status`, `--source`, `--limit`   |
| `swamp issue get <number>`    | Fetch and display issue details (title, type, status, author, body, assignees, comment count) |
| `swamp issue edit <number>`   | Edit title, body, or type of an existing issue (author or admin only)                         |
| `swamp issue bug`             | Title, description, steps to reproduce, environment                                           |
| `swamp issue feature`         | Title, problem statement, proposed solution, alternatives                                     |
| `swamp issue security`        | Title, description, reproduction, affected components, impact                                 |
| `swamp issue ripple <number>` | Free-form markdown body (no title); alias: `swamp issue comment`                              |

**Basic non-interactive examples:**

```bash
swamp issue search vault
swamp issue search --type bug --status open
swamp issue search --source swamp --limit 10 --json
swamp issue get 42
swamp issue get 42 --json
swamp issue edit 42
swamp issue edit 42 --title "Updated title"
swamp issue edit 42 --title "Updated title" --body "Updated body" --json
swamp issue edit 42 --type security
swamp issue bug --title "CLI crashes on empty input" --body "When running..." --json
swamp issue feature --title "Add dark mode" --body "I'd like..." --json
swamp issue security --title "..." --body "..." --json
swamp issue bug --email --title "Crash report" --body "Details..."
swamp issue ripple 184 --body "See also #183 for the related finding." --json
swamp issue ripple 327 --body "Fixed in latest build" --close --json
swamp issue ripple 42 --body "Re-opening per discussion" --reopen
swamp issue comment 184 --body "See also #183."
```

For detailed walkthroughs of each operation, see [reference.md](reference.md).

content.text: Ownership is swamp's own CLI (the quality rubric and push dry-run checks), so this goes in with no `--extension`. Filing:

input.command:
S=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-sme-src-webframp-swamp-extensions/5370cfa6-5fe1-4ed2-aae7-fa58150d12f1/scratchpad; cat > $S/issue.md <<'EOF'
## Summary

`swamp extension quality` and `swamp extension push --dry-run` pass extensions whose README and manifest description tell users to put secrets in plaintext, or to use vault reference syntax that swamp does not support. Both extensions below score `passed` / 100%. The dry run raises one warning, about the missing adversarial review, and nothing about secrets. Swamp's own model already says secrets come from a vault through `${{ vault.get(...) }}`. The published docs are what users copy, and the checks never read them for that.

## How we found it

In webframp/swamp-extensions#513 (merged) we audited the repo by hand and found plaintext-secret guidance in the shipped docs of most extensions that take credentials. The fix touched 121 extensions. Every one of them had passed the quality rubric and push checks, and had been published to the registry. The rubric did not catch a single case; a manual grep did.

Patterns we found in published README.md files and manifest `description` Quick Starts:

1. **Literal or placeholder value for a sensitive global arg:**
   `--global-arg apiToken=REDACTED (cloudflare-audit, the root README, the fal.ai and Datadog generators).
2. **Secret on the command line, so it lands in shell history:**
   `swamp vault put my-vault artifactory-token "eyJ..."` (artifactory). The example is also token-shaped.
3. **Reference syntax that swamp does not support:** `vault://my-vault/artifactory-token`, `<vault:x/y>`, `{{ vault "…" }}` (artifactory, reddit, gcp, azure, the vault extensions). Swamp refuses these for a sensitive global arg and passes them through as literal strings elsewhere. A user who follows the doc hits an error, then pastes the real token to make it work.
4. **Secret exported into the environment:** `export GITLAB_TOKEN="REDACTED"` (bench). The value leaves the vault and is not redacted.
5. **Describe strings that teach the wrong syntax:** the artifactory `token` global arg was described as `"vault:// reference to JFrog Identity Token"`. That text ships in the schema, and `push --dry-run` echoes it under `resolved.models[].globalArguments`.

## Reproduction

With swamp `20261021.155838.0-sha.f979f7c1`, at the commit before the fix:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/webframp/swamp-extensions && cd swamp-extensions
git checkout a2623fff
cd artifactory          # or cloudflare-audit
swamp repo init
swamp extension quality manifest.yaml --json   # → status: passed, percentage: 100
swamp extension push manifest.yaml --dry-run --yes
```

Observed:

- `quality`: `passed`, 100%. `has-readme`, `readme-example` and `rich-readme` all earn their points. The README example the rubric rewards is the one with the plaintext or invalid secret.
- `push --dry-run`: the only review warning is `"Adversarial review" — No adversarial review recorded`. The review skeleton has a `credentials-secrets` dimension, but it is self-attested, starts at `pending`, and `--yes` waives it. No deterministic check reads the docs.

Expected: both commands flag these docs, at least as a warning on the dry run and preferably as a rubric failure, because the user-facing setup path they describe puts a secret in plaintext or does not work.

## Why this matters

- **The README is the setup path.** Code can mark an arg `sensitive: true` (artifactory did), but if the doc says `--global-arg apiToken=REDACTED or `swamp vault put v K "<value>"`, the secret ends up in shell history, `.swamp.yaml`, or run history regardless.
- **The rubric rewards it.** `readme-example` gives a point for exactly the snippet that leaks.
- **The checks already parse what they need.** `push --dry-run` resolves the global-arg schema, including which args are sensitive, and bundles the README and manifest description. Matching docs against sensitive arg names needs nothing new.

## Suggested checks

A deterministic pass over the README, the manifest `description`, and schema describe strings:

- Invalid reference syntax: `vault://`, `<vault:`, `{{ vault `, `swamp vault set` (which does not exist).
- A `--global-arg` or `--input` for an arg the schema marks sensitive, or whose name matches `token|api_?key|secret|password`, set to anything other than a `${{ vault.get(...) }}` expression.
- `swamp vault put <vault> <KEY> <value>` with a value on the command line.
- Token-shaped literals: `sk-ant-`, `glpat-`, `ghp_`, `hvs.`, `eyJ`, `user:pass@`.
- `export <SECRET_NAME>=` in setup instructions.

Our repo-side versions of these greps live in the "Secrets Come From a Vault (HARD RULE)" section of the swamp-extensions `CLAUDE.md` added in #513. They are a workaround for a check that belongs in swamp, so every publisher gets it.

## Secondary observation

In the `push --dry-run --json` output, `resolved.models[].globalArguments[]` for artifactory's `token` lists `name`, `type`, `description` and `required` but not `sensitive`, although the source declares `.meta({ sensitive: true })`. If the registry and scorer read this resolved view, they cannot tell which args are secrets, which would also block the check proposed above.

content.text:
I filed it as **swamp-club Lab #3757**: https://swamp-club.com/lab/3757. It's a bug against the swamp CLI itself, since it's swamp's own quality and push checks that miss this.

**How I confirmed it:** I checked out `a2623fff`, the commit before PR #513, and ran the checks with swamp `20261021.155838.0` on two extensions whose docs leaked secrets:
- `cloudflare-audit` passed a literal value to the token argument: `--global-arg apiToken=REDACTED
- `artifactory` put the secret value on the command line with `swamp vault put … "eyJ..."`, and used `vault://`, a reference format swamp doesn't support.

Both scored `passed` / 100% on `swamp extension quality`. The README-example check even gave a point for the snippet that leaks. `push --dry-run` raised one warning, about the missing adversarial review. That review does have a credentials-secrets section, but you fill it in yourself and `--yes` waives it.

**What the issue covers:**
- The five patterns we fixed across 121 extensions in #513, with examples of each.
- The steps above, so anyone can reproduce it.
- Why the README matters even when the code marks the argument as sensitive: users follow the setup steps in the docs, not the code.
- Proposed checks over the README, the manifest description and the argument help text, based on the greps in our `CLAUDE.md`.
- A second finding: the `push --dry-run --json` output drops the `sensitive: true` flag from artifactory's `token` argument, even though the source sets it.

**One problem with what got posted:** swamp's own redaction filter treated two of my quoted examples as secrets: the `apiToken=REDACTED line and the bench `export GITLAB_TOKEN=REDACTED line. It replaced them with `[REDACTED-SECRET-n]` in the issue body. That's useful evidence, because swamp already detects these patterns but doesn't check published docs for them. So I added a comment saying so. I tried to word the comment so the filter would leave it alone, but it redacted that too, and two sentences in the middle came out garbled. The issue body still makes sense. If you want the comment fixed, I can post a cleaner one that describes the patterns without quoting them.

I removed the temporary worktree I used for the test, and nothing in the repo changed.
